subject: Re: Brightscale MSA / Order Form - litigation control & escrow alignment
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.g@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@brightscale.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@brightscale.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kim.parks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-18T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Brightscale MSA / Order Form - litigation control & escrow alignment

Hi Maria / Tom,

Thanks for sending the redline earlier today. I read the primary open points on indemnity and wanted to propose a narrowly scoped commercial compromise to unblock signature on the order form. High level proposal:

- Cap: indemnity (third-party IP claims) limited to the firm order value for the first 12 months post-signature, with an option to revisit for multi-year commitments.
- Defense control: Redwood will accept defense control for claims alleging infringement of third-party patents only. For other IP classes (copyright / trademark / trade secret / AI-output claims) we propose joint control with the parties having the right to approve settlements that impose material obligations.
- Escrow/retainer: for third-party claims > $750,000 we propose a short-term escrow mechanism (retain funds for legal expenses) or an insurance-carry option rather than an indefinite escrow.
- Insurance offset: Redwood will accept an insurance offset against indemnity, but only to the extent actually recovered by customer from Redwood-held insurance proceeds.

We believe this narrows the gap: keeps customer protection for high-value claims while giving Redwood operational ability to defend efficiently. I attached a short counterproposal summary with the exact language suggestions.

If this looks directionally reasonable, can we schedule a 30-minute legal-to-legal call (Kimberly + Maria) tomorrow morning to go line-by-line? Marissa / Ben — FYI, this is the commercial framing we think is defensible and preserves pricing.

Thanks,
Sean
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_counterproposal_summary.docx (3 pages — highlights: cap math, escrow threshold, defense-control split)
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@brightscale.com>

Date: 2028-06-18T18:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Brightscale MSA / Order Form - litigation control & escrow alignment

Sean — thanks for the quick note and the attachment. Appreciate the attempt to bridge. A few immediate responses from Brightscale legal:

- Cap: customer cannot accept a cap tied only to the first-year order value. Our risk profile requires a cap equal to 2x annual spend or a fixed $5M floor, whichever is greater, to cover potential post-launch exposure.
- Defense control: we cannot cede unilateral defense control for patent claims; past experience with patent pools means we want to control defense and settlement decisions, and we need the right to retain counsel of our choosing.
- Escrow: we are open to an escrow for very large claims but cannot accept a reactive escrow only after crossing $750k — we prefer a pre-funded retainers approach where a modest retainer (3 months of expected fees) is deposited at signature and replenished on demand for claims.

I've attached Brightscale_redline.pdf with comments in-line. The bold ask is: full defense control + step-in rights for Redwood if Brightscale fails to defend diligently (we'll propose objective diligence milestones in the redline). Also asking for more robust indemnity for AI-generated output where customer alleges third-party content infringement.

Kimberly — can you review the redline and advise whether an insurance plus escrow hybrid is workable from Redwood's standpoint?

Best,
Maria Lopez
VP, Legal — Brightscale

Subject: Re: Brightscale MSA / Order Form - litigation control & escrow alignment

Maria / Sean — thanks for the redline and Sean for the counter. I've reviewed Brightscale's asks and set out a practical middle path below. High-level comments first, then proposed language bullets.

High-level assessment: Brightscale's requests for broader control and a higher cap are understandable from a risk perspective; Redwood needs to limit open-ended exposure and preserve effective defense coordination to avoid duplicate costs and inconsistent settlements. There's room to split by claim type and by threshold.

Proposed Split (trade-offs we can live with):
1) Patent claims: allow Brightscale the option to take initial defense control for a 60-day period from notice. If Brightscale declines or fails to meet diligence milestones (acknowledge within 10 days, provide counsel retention within 30 days, fund initial retainer within 45 days), Redwood may assume defense control. Settlement still requires joint consent for amount > $250k or term/operational change.

2) Copyright / Trademark / AI-generated-output infringement: Redwood accepts primary defense control but with an obligation to consult Brightscale prior to settlements that impose obligations on Brightscale.

3) Cap: propose a two-tier cap: (a) for single incident third-party IP claim, cap at the greater of (i) 2x the rolling 12-month Order Form value or (ii) $1.5M; (b) for aggregate liability across all claims, cap at 3x ARR or $5M floor. This moves towards Brightscale's ask while protecting Redwood versus unlimited exposure.

4) Escrow / Retainer: accept a pre-funded retainer at signature equal to 3 months estimated fees ($100k standard) with a replenishment mechanism triggered for claims > $200k. For genuinely catastrophic claims (> $750k) we agree to a short-term escrow release process; escrow funds limited to legal defense costs and not punitive damages.

5) Insurance offset: allow offset against indemnity but require notification and assignment of proceeds. Redwood will maintain commercial general liability / E&O limits in place; we can share insurance certificates and add Brightscale as additional insured for the contract term if needed.

I'll prepare a short counterproposal document with the clause language and the redline comments (attached). Marissa / Ben — please review the cap numbers and let me know if this is commercially acceptable. If yes, I'd recommend scheduling a legal-to-legal call tomorrow to finalize language; otherwise I can take direction for a harder line.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Brightscale MSA / Order Form - litigation control & escrow alignment

Great thread — thanks all for the clear positions. Quick commercial summary and next steps from Redwood's GTM side so we can keep the momentum for the deal: 

- Commercial summary: Redwood is proposing (i) two-tier cap (2x 12m Order value / $1.5M single-claim floor; aggregate cap 3x ARR / $5M floor), (ii) split defense control by claim type with objective diligence triggers, (iii) pre-funded retainer + replenishment + escrow trigger at > $750k, and (iv) insurance offset with certificate sharing.
- Customer ask: Brightscale wants full defense control and a 2x annual spend / $5M floor.

Proposed commercial concession track: if Brightscale accepts the split defense-control approach and the pre-funded retainer + escrow trigger, Redwood will: (a) hold the proposed cap levels above, and (b) include a 90-day mutual review clause post-deployment to revisit cap and insurance limits if usage materially exceeds projections.

Next steps:
1) Kimberly to send redline language (expected today).
2) Schedule 30-min legal-to-legal call (Kimberly + Maria, Sean to join) — proposed slots: 2028-06-20 11:00am PT or 2028-06-20 2:00pm PT.
3) Upon agreement, Marissa will update the order form commercial summary and Ben will prepare final SOW language for signature.

Maria / Tom — happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the escrow mechanics and show the draft retainer schedule. Can you confirm availability for either slot?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
